findings.summary: The three base-revision value labels (14.16, 12.25, 24.62) are drawn in the series grey #929292 on white, measured at 3.11:1 contrast, against 5.28:1 for the head arm's labels and 19.7:1 for axis text. They are legible at the rendered size, but they are half of the comparison the figure exists to make and read markedly fainter than every other number on it.

rubric_items.contrast: Pass with one non-blocking finding. Axis and legend text 19.7:1 on white, head value labels 5.28:1; the base arm's three value labels are drawn in the bar grey at 3.11:1, legible but under 4.5:1.
rubric_items.data_ink: Pass. Two flat series fills (grey for the base arm, blue for this read) carry the weight; the rest is five y ticks, six value labels, three condition labels and the legend. No redundant encoding.
rubric_items.decoration: Pass. No gridlines, background fill, gradient, shading, shadow or bounding frame; a pixel scan finds only the two flat series colours plus anti-aliasing.
rubric_items.label_collision: Pass. No text pixel lies within 3 px of the canvas edge; the rotated y-axis label (x 20-41) clears the tick labels (x 49-71) by 8 px; the three condition labels are separated by 322 and 320 px, and the wrapped second line under the third group clears its first line and the canvas; each value label sits above its bar top with no pixel overlap and no two value labels are closer than 92 px.
rubric_items.legibility: Pass. Readable at a glance: three grouped conditions, every bar labelled with its value, y axis labelled 'peak resident memory [GiB]' ticked 0-25, a frameless two-entry legend above the panels, and each condition named in full under its group.
rubric_items.table_form: Pass. Three paired comparisons whose point is magnitude and ratio, not six values to look up; bars answer that reading better than a table.
